query: Make this go-to-market plan MECE, remove overlap between workstreams, and turn every item into a testable Definition of Done.
Is this MECE? Show me the gaps, overlaps, and the minimum repair.

Segment these accounts so every customer lands in one and only one segment, including unknown and transitional cases.
Audit this sales pipeline. Opportunities can currently appear in both qualified and proposal; define exclusive stages and exit criteria.
My board wants a five-slide answer-first deck on why churn increased. Deconstruct the problem into a MECE causal story before outlining slides.
Turn these launch notes into a sequenced operating plan with dependencies, owners, acceptance evidence, and failure paths.
Please repair this RACI. Several decisions have two accountable executives and some deliverables have no owner.
Build a decision tree for routing support incidents. Every case needs one path, including missing data and timeouts.
These categories mix channels, outcomes, and tasks. Reframe them using one basis and show the coverage ledger.
Check this project tracker for holes, duplicated work, unclear gates, and items with no accountable owner. Repair it so leadership can use it.
Convert these vague completion criteria into Boolean pass/fail standards with evidence, thresholds, approvers, and waiver rules.
Explain the definition of MECE in two sentences.
Please alphabetize these existing category labels without changing their meaning.
Translate the labels in this issue tree into Spanish. Keep the structure exactly as approved.
Use the approved outline to format a PowerPoint. Do not change the content hierarchy.
Summarize the text visible in this screenshot; no analysis or restructuring.
Make this workflow paragraph more concise and professional, but preserve every step as written.

Draw a Venn diagram showing overlap among product, sales, and customer success responsibilities; the overlap is intentional.

Group these book titles into fiction and nonfiction for a reading list. No audit or completeness analysis needed.
Apply consistent colors and fonts to this existing org chart without changing any boxes or reporting lines.
